notes: Taken from the Board of Elections' 46-day election notice, which lists every contest and issue, and the Board's sample ballots for each precinct, which give the full ballot wording and show which precincts vote on each issue (the notice gives no precinct lists for local issues).

Candidates are listed alphabetically by last name, not in ballot order: Ohio rotates the order of names from precinct to precinct. Certified write-in candidates are not printed on the ballot and are not listed.

"Where you live" uses the state voter file: a district or school levy is shown for a city, village or township when any of its voters live in that district. Your exact ballot depends on your precinct.
The Board's notice and sample ballots do not give local issue numbers.

issues.jurisdiction: McComb Local School District (Hancock, Putnam and Wood)
issues.title: School district income tax (0.25%) and bond issue ($23,815,000)
issues.area: McComb Local School District (Hancock, Putnam and Wood)

levy.purpose: Income tax for current expenses; bonds for constructing school facilities, including a new K-12 building.
levy.term: Income tax for a continuing period beginning January 1, 2027; bonds up to 37 years
levy.estimate: $23,815,000 principal; $245 for each $100,000 of market value

issues.text: Shall the McComb Local School District be authorized to do both of the following: 1. Impose an annual income tax of 0.25% on the school district income of individuals, for a continuing period of time, beginning January 1, 2027, for the purpose of current expenses? 2. Issue bonds for the purpose of constructing school facilities, including constructing a new K-12 building and including under a program of the Ohio Facilities Construction Commission, and renovating, repairing, improving and expanding existing school facilities; furnishing and equipping the same; improving the sites thereof; and acquiring real estate and interests therein in the principal amount of $23,815,000, to be repaid annually over a maximum period of 37 years, and levy a property tax outside the ten-mill limitation estimated by the county auditor to average over the bond repayment period 6.99 mills for each $1 of taxable value, which amounts to $245 for each $100,000 of the county auditor's market value, to pay the annual debt charges on the bonds, and to pay debt charges on any notes issued in anticipation of those bonds?
